target.statement: Horseshoe test MSE on the Diabetes dataset (n=442, p=10) is 0.472 ± 0.011, compared to Lasso 0.504 ± 0.057 and OLS 0.507 ± 0.060.

compute.basis: Diabetes is a 10-feature built-in dataset; the only real cost is a PyMC NUTS fit (2 chains × 3000 iters) on a tiny model, which the paper reports at ~12 s per fit, so a handful of seeds plus install time fits comfortably in well under an hour on CPU.

blockers: Repo may not contain the exact Diabetes script/config; some re-implementation of the PyMC Horseshoe model and 80/20 split may be needed
Exact seed set and split for the Diabetes table are not specified in the paper
title: Sparse Regression under Correlation and Weak Signals: A Reproducible Benchmark of Classical and Bayesian Methods
